claim: ASCON's lightweight design uses a 320-bit permutation bit-sliced into five 64-bit register words, providing 128-bit level security, and was declared the NIST Lightweight Cryptography standard winner in February 2023.
stance_target: establishes ASCON's algorithmic structure and standardization status as background for any student ASCON-on-FPGA project
scope_conditions: NIST Lightweight Cryptography standardization, finalized Feb 2023
quoted_support: ASCON's lightweight design utilizes a 320-bit permutation which is bit-sliced into five 64-bit register words, providing 128-bit level security... in Feb. 2023, the competition ended with ASCON as the winner.

claim: This survey is described by its authors as the first comprehensive academic review specifically covering the finalized 2023 NIST lightweight cryptography standard.
stance_target: positions this as the authoritative up-to-date related-work citation for a 2024-2026 ASCON FPGA student project
quoted_support: This survey is the first work on the current standard for lightweight cryptography, standardized in 2023.

claim: The survey systematically compares ASCON FPGA and ASIC hardware implementations on area, power, throughput, energy, and efficiency, alongside a review of differential and side-channel attacks (algebraic, cube/cube-like, forgery, fault injection, power analysis) and their countermeasures.
stance_target: gives a student project ready-made related-work framing dimensions (area/power/throughput/energy/efficiency) and security-analysis angle needed for IEEE/Scopus publishability
scope_conditions: survey scope across ASCON implementation and cryptanalysis literature
quoted_support: This work summarizes the different implementations of ASCON on field-programmable gate array (FPGA) and ASIC hardware platforms on the basis of area, power, throughput, energy, and efficiency overheads. The presented work also reviews various differential and side-channel analysis attacks (SCAs)... as well as the countermeasures for these attacks.

claim: ASCON is positioned as the lightweight dual to the legacy AES-GCM NIST standard for symmetric-key cryptography, targeting deeply-embedded systems such as implantable/wearable medical devices, smart fabrics, smart homes, and RFID tags.
stance_target: motivates real-world application framing (medical/IoT) for a student ASCON project's introduction/motivation section
quoted_support: This lightweight cryptographic standard will be used in deeply-embedded architectures to provide security through confidentiality and integrity/authentication (the dual of the legacy AES-GCM block cipher which is the NIST standard for symmetric key cryptography).
